what: Can our LSM model (lsm.glb, the exact CAD the generator tests with) be taken apart in the order of TechBox's published Cadasio take-apart (19075)? One entry per published step, from feasibility.py (log: feasibility_log.txt, raw numbers: feasibility.json) and the published replay (published_walk.py -> published_frames.json). 21 Oct 2026.
verdicts: FREE: nothing in the way. LATCH: held where it is by a barb, hook, lip or latch head, met within the first 0.5 mm; released by hand in the kit (the published guide marks these with an inset and red boxes); the move is otherwise clear. BLOCKED: runs into something later along the way.
published_moves_in_our_frame: From the replay: stems +Y 62.5, D8 +Y 54.1, D7 +Y 67.8, D5 +X 54.1, D4 -X 75.2, D11_C/D11_D +Y 86.5/88.8, D11_A/D11_B +Y 84.5/70.5, D6 +Y 44.7, matrix shown at +56.6 (= our P_HELD) then at [-90.76, 5.89, 25.09] (= our P_OUTSIDE, D10 still on it), D9s +Y 54.4, D10 -Y 48.4 off the held matrix, the three connectors +Z 30.5, D3 -Z 38.4, D2 shown 57.1 out (= our D2_OUT), nut -Z 85, button +Z 94.8, USB no motion (arrow +Z 63.3), R330 +Y 30.3, CAP +Y 29.1, R12K +Y 31.3, Nano +Y 31.

steps.detail: stand-in rods at most 0.2 mm off their 3.30 mm square holes in D6, D7, D8 (tight)

the four D11 latch heads, met at 0.07 mm: D8's slots (5.56 mm) are already 1.19 mm short of each post's neck on each side (README Q17); just above D8 the head reaches 2.27 mm past the slot edge, over a 1.06 mm spring cut
steps.fix: none needed; same as the Full Build's Step 38 reversed; the published inset of a corner latch is the cue

steps.detail: the latch barbs on D2's and D3's end tabs: 0.95 mm (lower prong) and 1.21 mm (upper) past D5's slot edges, starting 0.09 mm outside D5's outer face (contact at 0.2 - 0.3 mm); D1's tabs and D10's end tight (0.12, 0.21 mm); clear of D6, the D11s, the D9s, the matrix and its wires
steps.fix: none needed (published inset 'D5 / D3', red boxes on these tabs)

steps.detail: the barbs on D2's and D3's end tabs, 1.08 mm past D4's slot edges, starting 0.43 mm outside D4's face; D10's end 0.03 mm (tight, open-topped slot), D1 0.42 and D6 0.43 mm at rest (tight); clear of the matrix wires (all at x > 604) and of the USB cable, which stays in the notch for the whole 75.2 mm; D4 then lifts off the cable (+Y 65 free after -X 8 or -X 75.2)
steps.fix: none needed; the Full Build's way (-X 8, then up 65) meets the same barbs in its first 8 mm

steps.detail: LATCH at D1 (the tab's barb, 1.08 mm, under D1, on prongs with a 1.56 mm spring cut, contact 0.02 mm); then after 41.56 mm (35.2 once the tabs are out of D1) the same barb meets D6's corner slot, which is as long as D1's (10.32 mm against the barb's 11.06)
steps.fix: (a) once the tabs are pushed up out of D1 (6.38), lift the four posts and D6 together, 80 up: FREE (merges published 6, 7, 8); or (b) keep the published pairs and give the posts a hand path, the barb passing D6's slot edge by 1.1 mm for 3 mm, as the Full Build's Steps 34 - 35 brought them down (riders, never checked). D6 cannot go first: the posts' bodies above it are 2.78 mm wider than its corner slots on each side

steps.detail: lift clear of the D9s (D10 over them, 0.28 mm tight), D2, D3; P_HELD -> P_LIFT -> P_OUTSIDE and the straight line both clear; at P_OUTSIDE clear of the USB cable and its A end. But D10, still on the matrix, lies across our LIFT (routes 56 - 58) and OUTSIDE (53 - 55) wire shapes (1.1 - 1.5 mm: the wires pass through its plate; the Full Build drew them with D10 off); HELD (59 - 61) is clear of it. And OUTSIDE drapes over D4's top edge, which is gone by then
steps.fix: draw LIFT and OUTSIDE shapes with D10 on and D4 off; or take D10 off while the matrix is held (our draft), out of the published order

steps.detail: a detent lip at the top of each notch in D2 and D3 (notch 1.92 mm wide at y 901 - 902.5 against D9's 3.0 mm: 0.93 mm), contact 0.1 - 0.4 mm; clear of the OUTSIDE wires and the matrix aside

with the USB plug still in: the purple pin is 3.4 mm and its wire 4.5 mm clear of the plug in the current model (README question 2 and plan_final.md fact 4, the 0.3 mm clash, are out of date); clear of the button's leads
steps.fix: each wire then needs a loose shape (the Full Build has none)

steps.detail: D10's hook tips over the matrix board's edges: 1.14 mm (D5 end), 0.42 mm (D4 end), met at 0.16 - 0.23 mm. The Full Build's Step 31 reversed (+Z 40, then down 22) is also a LATCH (matrix material at the D5-end edge at 0.39 mm), then free; -Z is BLOCKED (the connectors at 11.7 mm)

D1's latch at D2's bottom (about 1.2 mm, contact 0.4 - 0.5 mm); clear of the USB plug and cable (still in), the Nano and the parts on the breadboard; the button's pins come straight up out of j5 and j16 with the USB plug in

in that order; the Nano before the 12 kOhm resistor would be a LATCH (the resistor's body over the Nano's edge, 0.4 mm)

wires_against_the_walls: Matrix wires as seated (routes 65 - 67, r 0.62) against D5 +X 54.1 and D4 -X 75.2: clear. USB cable (route 41, r 1.75) against D4 -X 75.2: clear, in the notch all the way; D4 lifts off it afterwards.
generator: tools/stepgen.blocked() flags the LATCH moves of D8, D5, D4, the D9s, D10, D3, D2 and the USB plug (points further back in a wall meet the barb beyond its 1.2 mm snug_fit) and passes the stems and a D11 post on its own (it does flag the posts' second stage through D6); but remove()'s warning fires only when the Full Build's own way was clear against what the Full Build tested it with, and hand-given ways are not order-checked; the D11 posts ride on D1 (no record), so their way must be given by hand.
